How to read this report

Every result carries one of three labels. They tell you how much weight the result can bear.

Exploratory  Describes the data. No hypothesis was tested.

Statistically supported  Result of a formal test with error control, valid under the model's assumptions.

Biological interpretation  A hypothesis linking results to prior knowledge. Needs independent validation.

All numbers, tables and figures below were produced by the analysis run named above and are stored with it.

Summary

PDC000127: CPTAC CCRCC Discovery Study - Proteome (160 samples), 154 samples was analysed with the Proteomics workflow (version 1.0.0) on the LSMA Analysis Lab. To find which proteins differ between 'tumour' and 'normal' (column 'tissue'), adjusting for patient. In summary, 860 proteins passed the thresholds. 2 point(s) are flagged under Limitations and should be read before the results are used.

  • 860 proteins passed the thresholds.

Introduction

From a table of protein intensities (MaxQuant, FragPipe, DIA-NN or a plain matrix) to quality control, normalisation and treatment of missing values, exploration, differential abundance and pathway analysis. Processing of raw mass spectra is done before the data reaches this workflow. The data analysed here is of kind 'protein_table'.

Aim

To find which proteins differ between 'tumour' and 'normal' (column 'tissue'), adjusting for patient.

Protein abundance per gene (log2 ratios) from the CPTAC common data analysis pipeline. 160 of 208 samples (80 Primary Tumor, 80 Solid Tissue Normal); 9,591 genes. https://pdc.cancer.gov/pdc/study/PDC000127 Cite the study's publication and the Proteomic Data Commons.

Methods

Assembled from what each completed stage recorded. Check it against the parameter tables below before using it in a write-up.

Protein intensities of 154 samples were read from PDC000127_protein_abundance.tsv.gz (plain matrix): 9,591 protein groups after removing 0 contaminants, 0 decoys and 0 proteins identified only by site. Scale: the table was already on a log scale and is used as it is.

Of 160 uploaded samples, 154 took part in the comparison of 'tissue' (normal, tumour); 6 samples were excluded by the analyst for the reasons listed under Data input.

Proteins were kept when quantified in at least 66% of the samples of at least one group of 'tissue', leaving 8,801 of 9,591.

Normalisation: median centring: every sample is shifted so that its median equals the mean of the medians. Missing values (2% of the table): MinProb (imputeLCMD): random draws from a narrow distribution around the 0.01 quantile of each sample, for values missing because they fall below the detection limit.

Differential abundance was tested with limma (empirical Bayes moderated t-test, intensity-dependent variance trend) on log2 intensities using the design ~ patient + tissue for the contrast tumour vs normal. P-values were adjusted with the BH method; proteins with adjusted p-value below 0.05 and an absolute log2 fold change of at least 1 were called. 0 called proteins were measured in one group only.

Pathway analysis (clusterProfiler over-representation and fgsea) used MSigDB 2026.1.Hs via msigdbr (collections: hallmark, go_bp, go_cc) against a background of the 8,801 quantified proteins with a gene name.

Random seed: 42. Software: R 4.5.2; Bioconductor 3.21; clusterProfiler 4.16.0; data.table 1.18.6.1; fgsea 1.34.2; impute 1.82.0; imputeLCMD 2.1; jsonlite 2.0.0; limma 3.64.3; msigdbr 26.1.1.

Analyses were run on the LSMA Analysis Lab (workflow 'proteomics' version 1.0.0).

Results

One section per stage, in the order they ran. The badge on each heading says how far its output can be taken: exploratory output describes the data, statistically supported output carries a test, and interpretation is a reading of either.

Stage 1 of 6

Data input Exploratory

A mass spectrometer measures peptides, the pieces a protein is cut into. Software such as MaxQuant, FragPipe or DIA-NN identifies the peptides, assembles them into proteins and reports an intensity per protein and sample. This stage reads that table, removes entries that are not real findings (common contaminants such as keratin and trypsin, decoy sequences used to estimate the error rate, proteins identified only by a modified peptide), treats a zero as "not quantified", and takes the logarithm of the intensities.

Sample preparation

Comparison: tissue, groups normal, tumour (reference: normal). Paired by patient. Adjusted for: patient. These choices were made before the analysis and the uploaded files were not changed.

How to interpret this stage

Check how many proteins remain and how many values are missing. A few thousand proteins from cells or tissue is typical; a pull-down experiment has fewer, and many missing values in the control are expected there.

How to interpret this stage

If proteins with missing values are clearly less intense than complete ones, the values are missing because they fall below the detection limit ("missing not at random"). If the two distributions coincide, values are missing by chance. Most datasets are a mixture, dominated by the first kind.

Stage 3 of 6

Normalisation and missing values Exploratory

Normalisation removes differences between runs that come from the amount of sample loaded and the state of the instrument. Imputation replaces missing values with plausible numbers so that every protein can be compared between groups.

Note. These values look like log ratios to a reference (centred near zero), as in TMT or iTRAQ data. There a missing value seldom means 'below the detection limit', and MinProb fills it with a strongly negative ratio. Consider k-nearest neighbours (knn) or no imputation for this dataset.

Key numbers

Stage 5 of 6

Differential abundance Statistically supported

For every protein a linear model is fitted to the log2 intensities and the two groups are compared with limma's moderated t-test, which borrows information across proteins to steady the variance estimates when replicates are few. P-values are corrected for the number of proteins tested.

How to interpret this stage

A protein is called when its adjusted p-value is below the threshold and it changes at least two-fold (by default). The table says how many values of each group were filled in. In the demonstration pull-down, the proteins far to the right of the volcano plot are the partners that bind ubiquitin chains.

Stage 6 of 6

Pathway analysis Biological interpretation

The proteins are mapped to genes by the gene names in the protein table. Gene sets are tested for over-representation among the differential proteins and, with GSEA, for sitting at the top or bottom of the list ranked by the test statistic.

Note. The background is the proteins that were quantified, not all genes. A mass spectrometer sees abundant proteins best, so sets of abundant proteins are easier to find enriched.

Discussion

What the run amounts to, drawn from the stages that carry a judgement. Every sentence below was written by the stage that reached it; none is a later interpretation.

This run describes the data rather than testing a hypothesis about it, so there is no verdict to draw together here. The Results describe what was measured.

The run raised 2 warnings, listed with the stages that raised them. They are part of the result, not notes beside it.

Everything above was produced by Proteomics on the data named in the Data section, with the parameters recorded under each stage. The Limitations section says what this design cannot show, and should be read before any of this is quoted.

Limitations

Everything the analysis flagged about itself, gathered in one place. Each one limits what the results above can be used for.
